    "title": "Exponential anticoncentration conjecture for random spanning trees",
    "statement": "Let $\\varepsilon>0$ be real. The stated exponential scale is best possible up to lower-order terms, while extension to suitable $(n,d,\\lambda)$-graphs is posed as an additional direction.",

  "372532": {

    "title": "The topological exactness conjecture for hard telic problems",
    "statement": "Let $(X,T)$ be an efficiently discretizable topological dynamical system. Recall that $T$ is **topologically exact** if, for every nonempty open set $U\\subset X$, there exists $n_0\\in\\mathbb{N}$ such that $T^{n_0}(U)=X$. A telic problem is called hard-on-average when it satisfies the stated almost-everywhere average-case hardness condition.\n\n**Topological exactness conjecture.** If $T$ is topologically exact and the system admits a hard telic problem, then there exists an almost-everywhere $\\delta$ hard-on-average telic problem coming from the dynamical system.\n\nThe conjecture is motivated by the possible construction of one-way functions from dynamical systems with hard telic problems. Its resolution is not supplied in the source.",

    "statement": "For a bridgeless graph $G$, let\n\n$$\nS_p^{d-1}:=\\{\\boldsymbol{x}\\in\\mathbb{R}^d:\\lVert\\boldsymbol{x}\\rVert_p=1\\}\n$$\n\nbe the unit $p$-sphere. **The generalized $S^2_p$-flow conjecture.** For every bridgeless graph $G$ and every $p\\in[1,\\infty]$,\n\n$$\n\\phi_{3,p}(G)=2.\n$$\n\nThis extends Jain's $S^2$-flow conjecture from the Euclidean sphere to all $p$-norms.
